Archimedes

# AI agents that design physical things.

Give it an engineering goal. A swarm of agents writes designs as code, tests every one in a real physics simulator, and keeps improving the best. When a result doesn't hold up, it says so.

## It starts with a few ideas.

A stock drone propeller, six very different starting designs the agents wrote as code, and their first two tries.

## Then the agents get to work.

Each one writes a new design, simulates it in air and in water, and builds on whatever scores well.

## 1,251 designs in 12 hours.

Six teams of agents on 12 cloud machines, borrowing each other's best ideas. The run starts in the top-left corner and grows outward. The blue deepens as it goes: the designs kept getting better.

## Then it picks the best one.

The winner is design 1,255. Before calling it a result, Archimedes re-checks it on finer simulations.

## One propeller that flies and swims.

- Swept blades. One agent grafted a swept tip onto the best paddle blade; that idea spread to every team and won.

- One blade, two settings. The hub twists it flatter for air and steeper for water, and a 6:1 gear keeps the motor in its efficient range underwater.

- ~90% of a specialist propeller in each fluid, from a single rotor.

## Seven real problems. Here's what happened.

Underwater, a stock prop stalls its motor. Archimedes redesigned blade and gearbox together.

### An AI data hall, cooled for less.

Cooling ran flat out and its hottest rack still overheated. The cheap fix gets 79% of the savings for under a quarter of the cost.

## It tells you when it's wrong.

Every leading design gets re-tested on a finer simulation. When something doesn't hold up, the report says so.

- Drone propeller: its first answer optimized the wrong thing. The first search tuned the blade on its own. Checked against the real motor, its score collapsed, so Archimedes rewrote the goal and searched again.

- Data hall: the first winner wasn't buildable. It assumed the 2008 cooling coils could run warmer water than they can. Verification caught it; the second search built that limit in.

- Crucible purge: true only when cold. A 2,500 °C check erased most of the advantage, so it's labelled a cold-flow result.
